info.title: ABI Validate — MCP Tool Reference
info.description: The 7 ABI Validate MCP tools' request/response schemas. The two internal upload-panel tools (`upload_validation_asset_bytes` and `finalize_validation_upload_session`) are excluded — they are called by the MCP-Apps upload panel itself, not by integrators. ABI Validate is an MCP server: every real call goes over a single JSON-RPC endpoint at /mcp, not per-tool HTTP routes. The per-tool `POST /tools/<name>` paths documented below are a DOCUMENTATION CONVENTION only — one synthetic operation per registered MCP tool, so a human reader can see each tool's request/response shape in a familiar OpenAPI/Swagger viewer. They are not callable HTTP routes: do not run client codegen against this document and expect the result to work against /mcp.

post.summary: See the asset input shape a validate_asset call needs. Call
post.description:
See the asset input shape a validate_asset call needs. Call
            this FIRST, before validate_asset, on a host unfamiliar with the
            ABI Validate feature (Adobe Brand Intelligence).

            Inputs: none.
            Returns: allowed source values plus guidance on media_type and
            the bulk (list of assets) shape validate_asset expects.
            Next: build one or more asset inputs and pass them to validate_asset.

schema.description:
get_validation_options result — the asset-input shape validate_asset
expects. Static (not tenant-fetched): there is no catalog endpoint for this.

source_type_note.default: 'web' takes a public or presigned http(s) URL directly in `value`. 'blob' takes an `asset_id` staged via prepare_validation_asset_upload or upload_validation_asset_bytes — pass the id straight through, no separate download-URL resolution step needed.
source_type_note.title: Source Type Note

media_type_note.default: media_type is the asset's MIME type (e.g. image/png, application/pdf) — not a fixed enum; send whatever MIME type matches the asset.
media_type_note.title: Media Type Note

bulk_note.default: validate_asset takes a LIST of assets (1 or more) and starts one invocation that checks all of them — never call it once per asset.
bulk_note.title: Bulk Note

schema.title: ValidationOptions

post.summary: Get a validation invocation's per-item results: each item's
post.description:
Get a validation invocation's per-item results: each item's
            status, summary, and any brand-guideline violations found. Call
            this to report a finished invocation — you are the only reporter
            of results, so poll get_validation_status yourself until terminal,
            then call this once.

            Inputs: invocation_id (from validate_asset).
            Returns: the invocation's overall status plus every item's full
            result — item_id, status, summary, violations (empty means no
            violations found for that item), and the asset image
            (asset_url/asset_data_url).
            Next: if the invocation is not yet terminal, poll
            get_validation_status again shortly instead of calling this.

schema.description: get_validation_result result. ``status`` mirrors the invocation's own lifecycle. ``items`` carries every item's full per-item result — fetched in one call so the model never has to loop tool calls per item. ``asset_data_url`` is a same-origin ``data:`` URI of each item's image, best-effort (``None`` on fetch failure, oversize, or a non-image asset) — prefer it over ``asset_url`` when rendering, since a UI-capable host's iframe CSP commonly blocks a remote ```` even when the URL itself is perfectly reachable.
schema.title: ValidationResult

post.summary: Lightweight poll target for in-flight invocations — overall status
post.description:
Lightweight poll target for in-flight invocations. Both the live
            progress panel and the model should poll this to track a running
            validation invocation. It returns the invocation's overall status
            plus a per-item status summary (no violations, no full-resolution
            image — each item's thumbnail is included), so it is cheap enough
            to poll every few seconds while items are in flight. Once
            terminal, use get_validation_result instead (it also returns
            each item's violations and full-resolution asset image).

            Inputs: invocation_id (from validate_asset).
            Returns: invocation_id, overall status, item_count,
            success_count, failure_count, and per-item status summaries.

schema.description:
get_validation_status result — the invocation's overall status plus a
per-item status summary, nothing else. The progress panel's poll target:
no violations, no asset images (get_validation_result fetches and
base64-encodes those per item, which is not something to redo every few
seconds). The model may poll this too while waiting, but should read
get_validation_result once the invocation is terminal for the full report.
schema.title: ValidationStatus

post.summary: Poll this after open_validation_asset_upload instead of
post.description:
Poll this after open_validation_asset_upload instead of
            waiting for a chat message from the panel — some hosts refuse to
            let a widget send one. Poll silently, exactly like
            get_validation_status, until settled is true. "Poll" means call
            this tool again yourself, each time — never a shell command,
            sleep loop, or reading a cached tool-result file off disk; none
            of those re-run the tool, so none of them can ever see settled
            flip to true.

            Inputs: upload_session_id (from open_validation_asset_upload).
            Returns: settled (false while the panel's batch is still
            uploading) and assets (each staged file's asset_id, media_type,
            asset_name — ready to pass straight to validate_asset).
            Next: if settled is false, poll again shortly. Once true, use
            assets for validate_asset; an empty list means every upload in
            the batch failed.

schema.description:
``settled`` is false until the panel's current upload batch finishes
(``finalize_validation_upload_session``) — the model should keep polling
until it flips true, then use ``assets`` for ``validate_asset``. An empty
``assets`` list with ``settled: true`` means every file in the batch
failed to upload.
schema.title: ValidationUploadStatus

post.summary: Open an inline panel to upload LOCAL creative files for ABI
post.description:
Open an inline panel to upload LOCAL creative files for ABI
            Validate (Adobe Brand Intelligence) brand-compliance validation
            (drag-and-drop, multiple files — they'll all validate together in
            one bulk invocation). DEFAULT to this whenever the user hasn't
            given an asset yet — no URL, no path, no attachment in their
            message, even a bare "validate this" — open the panel
            immediately rather than asking a text question first. If they
            already gave a concrete local path, call
            prepare_validation_asset_upload directly instead — do not open
            this panel just to ask the user to re-drag a file whose path
            they already gave you. Never ask the user to paste asset JSON
            themselves.

            Inputs: none.
            Returns: opens the panel, plus an upload_session_id. Once you're
            done waiting on the panel, poll
            get_validation_upload_status(upload_session_id) yourself,
            silently, until it reports settled: true — do not wait for a
            chat message from the panel, some hosts refuse to let it send
            one. On a host that can't render the panel, the message instead
            points at prepare_validation_asset_upload.
            Next: once settled, pass its assets to validate_asset as
            assets: [{source: "blob", asset_id, media_type, asset_name}, ...].

schema.description:
``upload_session_id`` is what the model polls
``get_validation_upload_status`` with — the panel tags every file it
stages with this same id, so the model never has to wait on a host-pushed
chat turn to learn what was uploaded.
schema.title: OpenValidationAssetUploadResult

post.summary: Prepare to validate a LOCAL file with ABI Validate (Adobe
post.description:
Prepare to validate a LOCAL file with ABI Validate (Adobe
            Brand Intelligence). This is the DEFAULT for a local file once
            you already have its exact path (the user typed or pasted it) —
            prefer this over open_validation_asset_upload's drag-and-drop
            panel in that case, on any host: asking the user to re-drag a
            file whose path they already gave you is redundant. For a
            public URL or presigned URL, pass it straight to validate_asset
            instead.

            Inputs: local_path (used only to build the command — the server
            never reads your disk) and content_type.
            Returns: an upload ticket with a ready-to-run upload_command.
            Next: run upload_command locally, confirm it exits 0 (a nonzero
            exit means the PUT failed — do not proceed), then pass the
            returned asset_id to validate_asset as one entry in assets:
            {source: "blob", asset_id, media_type, asset_name}.

schema.description:
A presigned upload target + a ready-to-run command for a Validate asset.

Run ``upload_command`` locally and confirm it exits 0, then pass
``asset_id`` to validate_asset as
``{source: "blob", asset_id, media_type, asset_name}``. If ``expires_at``
lapses first, re-mint via prepare_validation_asset_upload.
schema.title: ValidationAssetUploadTicket

post.summary: Start an ABI Validate (Adobe Brand Intelligence) brand-
post.description:
Start an ABI Validate (Adobe Brand Intelligence) brand-
            compliance validation invocation for one or more creative assets.

            Bulk by design: pass every asset the user wants checked in ONE
            call's assets list — never call this once per asset. Use
            get_validation_options first if the asset input shape is unfamiliar.

            Inputs: a ValidateAssetRequest — assets: a list of one or more,
            each one of {source: "web", media_type, value, asset_name} for an
            already-reachable (or presigned) URL, or {source: "blob",
            asset_id, media_type, asset_name} for a file staged via
            prepare_validation_asset_upload / open_validation_asset_upload /
            upload_validation_asset_bytes. Optional campaign_id — omit it
            unless the user has one to give you; if the tenant requires an
            explicit one, the call fails with a clear error naming what's
            missing rather than guessing.
            Returns: invocation_id and item_count.
            Next: automatically poll get_validation_status yourself,
            repeatedly and silently, until the invocation's status is
            completed or failed — do not narrate each check in the chat.
            "Poll" means call get_validation_status again yourself, each
            time — never a shell command, sleep loop, or reading a cached
            tool-result file off disk; none of those re-run the tool, so
            none of them can ever see a status change. Some hosts also draw
            a progress panel; it is a decorative visual for the user and
            hands you nothing, so never wait on it instead of polling. Once
            terminal, call get_validation_result exactly once for the full
            per-item report, then stop — do not poll again for this
            invocation afterward.

schema.description:
validate_asset result. ``invocation_id`` is the one id to poll with —
the model is always the one to track and report the run (see
get_validation_status / get_validation_result); a progress panel, when a
host renders one, is a decorative visual only and never a substitute for
polling.
schema.title: ValidateAssetResult

AttributionSummary.description:
A pointer either into the validated asset itself (asset attribution)
or into a brand-guideline document (corpus attribution — carries
presigned read URLs so a client can jump to the source).
AttributionSummary.title: AttributionSummary

BoundingBoxCoords.description:
A bounding box on the asset, normalized to 0-1 (the backend's region
model — independent of the asset's actual pixel dimensions, so the client
only needs the rendered image's own box).
BoundingBoxCoords.title: BoundingBoxCoords

RegionSummary.description:
Where a violation was found on the asset, if the backend attributed
it to a specific region.
RegionSummary.title: RegionSummary

ValidationItemResult.description:
One item's full result: status, summary, violations, and the asset
image for rendering (mirrors the asset as validated, not a fresh fetch).
ValidationItemResult.title: ValidationItemResult

ViolationSummary.description: One brand-guideline violation found on an item.
ViolationSummary.title: ViolationSummary

ValidationItemStatus.description:
One item's cheap status summary — no violations, no full-resolution
image. ``thumbnail_url`` is a small preview only, already present on the
raw item-summary response at no extra cost. ``thumbnail_data_url`` is
that same thumbnail fetched server-side and embedded as a data URL, same
trick as get_validation_result's ``asset_data_url`` — a plain remote
``thumbnail_url`` gets blocked by the panel's iframe CSP the same way, so
the panel prefers this field and falls back to a glyph placeholder only
when it's None (fetch failed, oversize, or not an image). The full-
resolution asset (rendition preferred) is still get_validation_result's
job — this is thumbnail-sized only.
ValidationItemStatus.title: ValidationItemStatus

StagedUploadAssetSummary.description:
One file staged through the upload panel — the exact shape
``validate_asset`` expects for a ``source: "blob"`` asset entry.
StagedUploadAssetSummary.title: StagedUploadAssetSummary

BlobAssetInput.description:
An asset staged via prepare_validation_asset_upload /
upload_validation_asset_bytes, referenced by its asset_id.
BlobAssetInput.title: BlobAssetInput

ValidateAssetRequest.description: Everything validate_asset needs to start a bulk validation invocation.
ValidateAssetRequest.title: ValidateAssetRequest

WebAssetInput.description: A public or presigned http(s) URL the backend fetches directly.
WebAssetInput.title: WebAssetInput
